records.source: וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃
records.gloss: And added Job to take up his discourse, and said:
pieces: Then Job took up his discourse again:

L.1: And Job again took up his discourse and said:

decisions.choice: discourse: a weighty, carefully shaped speech
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) can name a proverb, a parable or a taunt, but here, as in 27:1, it names a formal poetic speech. The same words open 27:1, and no friend speaks in between: Job goes on with his closing speech, which runs through chapter 31. This introduction, like the others in Job, stays prose.

decisions.choice: added to take up: spoke again, continued
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "he added to take up", a common way of saying that someone did something again (Genesis 8:12; Job 27:1). Job pauses and resumes; chapters 29-31 look back on his past (chapter 29), set it against his present (chapter 30), and end with his oath of innocence (chapter 31).

decisions.choice: took up his discourse again (B); went on speaking (R), without "and said"
alternatives: again took up his discourse and said
decisions.reason: As in the other speech introductions, Balanced and Readable say the speaking verb once; Readable puts the idiom plainly (m2).

records.heading: Job remembers the days when God watched over him

records.source: מִֽי־יִתְּנֵ֥נִי כְיַרְחֵי־קֶ֑דֶם כִּ֝ימֵ֗י אֱל֣וֹהַּ יִשְׁמְרֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Who will give me as [the] months of old, as [the] days [when] God watched over me,
pieces: Oh, that I were as in the months gone by, \q as in the days when God watched over me,

L.2: Who will give me [to be] as [in the] months of old, \q as [in the] days [when] God watched over me,

R.2: I wish I could go back to the months of long ago, \q to the days when God watched over me.

decisions.choice: Who will give me: an exclamation of longing, "if only"
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is the regular Hebrew way of voicing a wish (6:8; 14:4, 13; 19:23; 23:3). Job is not asking anyone; he longs for the past.

decisions.choice: watched over: kept and protected
decisions.reason: The verb (shamar) is the word for guarding and keeping (Numbers 6:24; Psalm 121:7). In 10:12 Job said God's care preserved his spirit; in 13:27 and 14:16 the same God now "watches" his steps to find fault.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on to verse 6
decisions.reason: Verses 2-6 are one long wish. Verses 3-6 each begin with "when" or "as" and describe the days Job longs for; the sentence ends in verse 6.

decisions.choice: Oh, that I were (B); I wish I could go back (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Hebrew wish into a form English uses for wishes (m1); Literal keeps the Hebrew question.

records.source: בְּהִלּ֣וֹ נֵ֭רוֹ עֲלֵ֣י רֹאשִׁ֑י לְ֝אוֹרוֹ אֵ֣לֶךְ חֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: when he made shine his lamp over my head, [by] his light I walked [through] darkness,
pieces: when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lamp shone above my head, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light I walked through the darkness,

L.3: when {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lamp shone over my head, \q [and by] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light I walked [through] darkness,

R.3: Then {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} lamp shone over my head, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} light showed me the way through the dark.

decisions.choice: made shine: God caused his lamp to shine
decisions.reason: The form comes from a verb meaning to shine (31:26; 41:10), not from the like-sounding verb "praise". God is the one who makes the lamp shine.

decisions.choice: his lamp, his light: God's favor and guidance
decisions.reason: A lamp over the head pictures a household lit and safe, under God's care (Psalm 18:29; Proverbs 20:27). Bildad said the lamp of the wicked goes out (18:5-6); Job remembers when God's lamp shone on him.

decisions.choice: [and by] his light ... through
decisions.reason: The second line has no "and" and no "through"; English needs both to make a sentence.

decisions.choice: showed me the way through the dark
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what walking by God's light means (m2).

records.source: כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר הָ֭יִיתִי בִּימֵ֣י חָרְפִּ֑י בְּס֥וֹד אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַּ עֲלֵ֣י אָהֳלִֽי׃
records.gloss: as I was in [the] days of my autumn, in [the] intimate counsel of God over my tent,
pieces: as I was in the days of my prime, \q when God's friendship was over my tent,

L.4: as I was in [the] days of my autumn, \q when [the] friendship of God [was] over my tent,

R.4: Then I was in the best years of my life, \q and God was a close friend to my family.

decisions.choice: my autumn: the ripe years of his life, his prime
decisions.reason: The word (choref) names autumn, the season of harvest in Israel's year (Genesis 8:22). Used of a life it means the years of full strength and fruit, not old age or early youth.

decisions.choice: intimate counsel: close friendship, the talk of trusted friends
decisions.reason: The word (sod) means a circle of trusted friends and the confidences shared in it (15:8; 19:19; Psalm 25:14). Job remembers God as a friend at home with him. The Greek translation reads a verb meaning "to shelter", which would give "when God sheltered my tent"; the Hebrew as it stands speaks of friendship.

decisions.choice: my tent: my household, my home
decisions.reason: "Tent" is an old word for one's home and household (5:24; 8:22; 18:6), even for someone who lived in a house (1:4, 13).

decisions.choice: my prime (B); the best years of my life (R)
decisions.reason: In English "autumn" of life suggests decline; the Hebrew picture is of harvest and strength (m1). Literal keeps "autumn".

records.source: בְּע֣וֹד שַׁ֭דַּי עִמָּדִ֑י סְבִ֖יבוֹתַ֣י נְעָרָֽי׃
records.gloss: when still [the] Almighty [was] with me, around me my young ones,
pieces: when the Almighty was still with me \q and my children were all around me,

L.5: when [the] Almighty [was] still with me, \q [and] my children [were] around me,

R.5: God All-Powerful was still with me then, \q and my children were around me.

decisions.choice: the Almighty: Shaddai, as in 5:17
decisions.reason: Job uses the old name Shaddai, rendered "the Almighty" throughout the book (see 5:17).

decisions.choice: my young ones: Job's children
decisions.reason: The word (na'ar) means a young person and is used both of children and of young servants. In the prologue it names the servants killed in the raids (1:15-17) and Job's children killed when the house fell (1:19). Here, after "the Almighty with me", the picture of a full home points to his children, who were all killed; the servants cannot be ruled out.

decisions.choice: God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable renders Shaddai as "God All-Powerful", as elsewhere in Job.

records.source: בִּרְחֹ֣ץ הֲלִיכַ֣י בְּחֵמָ֑ה וְצ֥וּר יָצ֥וּק עִ֝מָּדִ֗י פַּלְגֵי־שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: when [were] bathed my steps in curds, and [the] rock poured out beside me streams of oil!
pieces: when my steps were bathed in cream, \q and the rock poured out streams of olive oil for me!

L.6: when my steps were washed in curds, \q and the rock poured out beside me streams of oil!

R.6: Back then my path was so rich it was as if it were washed in cream, \q and even the rocks poured out rivers of olive oil for me.

decisions.choice: steps bathed in curds, rock pouring oil: overflowing plenty
decisions.reason: The pictures exaggerate on purpose: so much milk that his feet could be washed in it, so much oil that even rock gave it. Moses' song speaks of God giving Israel oil from the flinty rock and curds from the herd (Deuteronomy 32:13-14); Job 20:17 speaks of streams of honey and curds. The rock may also suggest the stone olive press.

decisions.choice: curds: thickened milk, cream or butter
decisions.reason: The word (chem'ah) means milk thickened into curds, cream or soft butter, a sign of rich pasture and many herds (Genesis 18:8; Isaiah 7:22).

decisions.choice: the wish of verses 2-6 ends here
decisions.reason: This is the last of the "when" lines that began in verse 3. Verses 7-25 go on to describe Job's place among his people.

decisions.choice: it was as if
decisions.reason: Readable signals that the line is a picture of plenty, not a literal event (m1).

records.source: בְּצֵ֣אתִי שַׁ֣עַר עֲלֵי־קָ֑רֶת בָּ֝רְח֗וֹב אָכִ֥ין מוֹשָׁבִֽי׃
records.gloss: When I went out [to the] gate by [the] town, in the square I prepared my seat,
pieces: When I went out to the city gate \q and took my seat in the public square,

L.7: When I went out [to the] gate by [the] city, \q [and] in the square I set up my seat,

R.7: When I went to the city gate \q and sat down in the meeting place,

decisions.choice: the gate and the square: the place of the town's council and court
decisions.reason: In Israelite towns the open space at the gate was where the elders met, cases were heard and business was witnessed (Ruth 4:1-2, 11; Deuteronomy 21:19). Taking a seat there means taking his place among the leading men of the town.

decisions.choice: town: a poetic word for city
decisions.reason: The word (qeret) is a rare, poetic word for a town or city (Proverbs 8:3; 9:3).

decisions.choice: verses 7-10 are one sentence
decisions.reason: Verse 7 sets the scene; verses 8-10 say what happened when Job arrived.

decisions.choice: the meeting place
decisions.reason: Readable says what the square was used for (m1).

records.source: רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וִֽ֝ישִׁישִׁים קָ֣מוּ עָמָֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: saw me young men and hid themselves, and aged [men] rose, stood;
pieces: the young men saw me and stepped aside, \q and the old men rose and stood;

L.8: young men saw me and hid themselves, \q and old men rose [and] stood;

R.8: the young men saw me and moved out of the way, \q and even the old men stood up for me.

decisions.choice: hid ... rose and stood: marks of respect
decisions.reason: The young men withdrew out of respect, and even the elders, who would normally be shown honor themselves, stood up and stayed standing for him (Leviticus 19:32 commands rising before the aged).

decisions.choice: aged men: the old men, the elders
decisions.reason: The word (yashish) means very old (12:12; 15:10). Men are meant: the council at the gate was made up of the town's men.

decisions.choice: stepped aside (B); moved out of the way (R)
decisions.reason: "Hid" would suggest fear; the sense is that they withdrew to make room for him (m1). Literal keeps "hid themselves".

records.source: שָׂ֭רִים עָצְר֣וּ בְמִלִּ֑ים וְ֝כַ֗ף יָשִׂ֥ימוּ לְפִיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: princes restrained words, and a palm they put on their mouth;
pieces: officials stopped talking \q and put their hands over their mouths;

L.9: princes held back words \q and put [their] hand on their mouth;

R.9: leaders stopped talking \q and covered their mouths with their hands.

decisions.choice: princes: men of rank, officials
decisions.reason: The word (sar) means a leader or official; here, men of standing in the town.

decisions.choice: hand on mouth: a gesture of silence
decisions.reason: Putting a hand over the mouth means keeping quiet, out of respect or awe (21:5; 40:4; Judges 18:19).

decisions.choice: officials (B); leaders (R)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere, sar is "princes" at Literal, "officials" at Balanced and "leaders" at Readable.

records.source: קוֹל־נְגִידִ֥ים נֶחְבָּ֑אוּ וּ֝לְשׁוֹנָ֗ם לְחִכָּ֥ם דָּבֵֽקָה׃
records.gloss: [the] voice of nobles was hidden, and their tongue to their palate stuck.
pieces: the voices of the nobles fell silent, \q and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.

L.10: the voice of nobles was hushed, \q and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.

R.10: Even important men went quiet, \q as if their tongues were stuck in their mouths.

decisions.choice: nobles: leading men
decisions.reason: The word (nagid) means a leader or prince, someone in front of others (31:37).

decisions.choice: tongue stuck to the palate: unable or unwilling to speak
decisions.reason: The picture is of a mouth dried shut (Psalm 137:6; Ezekiel 3:26). Here it means the nobles fell completely silent when Job came to speak.

decisions.choice: as if
decisions.reason: Readable marks the tongue line as a picture of silence (m2).

records.source: כִּ֤י אֹ֣זֶן שָׁ֭מְעָה וַֽתְּאַשְּׁרֵ֑נִי וְעַ֥יִן רָ֝אֲתָ֗ה וַתְּעִידֵֽנִי׃
records.gloss: For an ear heard and called me blessed, and an eye saw and bore witness for me.
pieces: When anyone heard me, they called me blessed, \q and when anyone saw me, they spoke well of me,

L.11: For [the] ear heard and called me blessed, \q and [the] eye saw and bore witness for me.

R.11: People who heard me said I was a happy man, \q and people who saw me spoke up for me.

decisions.choice: called me blessed: called me happy, counted my life fortunate
decisions.reason: The verb ('ashar) is related to the word "happy" in "Happy is the one" (Psalm 1:1); to call someone this is to say their life is good and favored (Genesis 30:13; Proverbs 31:28).

decisions.choice: bore witness for me: spoke up for me, gave a good report of me
decisions.reason: The verb ('ud) is a word of testimony. Those who saw what Job did testified in his favor; verses 12-17 say what they saw.

decisions.choice: For: verses 11-17 give the reason for the respect of verses 8-10
decisions.reason: The word ki links the honor Job was shown to what he did for the weak; verse 12 begins with the same word.

decisions.choice: anyone who heard / saw me (B); people who heard / saw me (R)
decisions.reason: Hebrew lets the ear and the eye stand for the people who heard and saw; Balanced and Readable name the people.

records.source: כִּֽי־אֲ֭מַלֵּט עָנִ֣י מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝יָת֗וֹם וְֽלֹא־עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: For I rescued [the] afflicted crying for help, and [the] fatherless and [one] not a helper to him.
pieces: because I rescued the poor who cried for help \q and the fatherless who had no one to help them.

L.12: For I rescued [the] poor [who] cried for help, \q and [the] fatherless and [the one who had] no helper.

R.12: This was because I rescued poor people who cried for help, \q and orphans who had no one to help them.

decisions.choice: the afflicted: the poor and downtrodden
decisions.reason: The word ('ani) means someone poor, bowed down and without power, often the victim of others (24:4, 9, 14). Eliphaz charged that Job had crushed such people (22:6-9); Job answers that he rescued them.

decisions.choice: the fatherless and the one with no helper: probably one group, the orphan who has no one
alternatives: two groups, the orphan and anyone without a helper
decisions.reason: Hebrew has "the fatherless and no helper to him". The "and" can join two kinds of people or describe the orphan further; Psalm 72:12 uses the same words of the poor man with no helper. The sense is close either way.

decisions.choice: because (B); This was because (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced runs verse 12 on from verse 11 as its reason (m3 on verse 11); Readable starts a new sentence and says so plainly.

records.source: בִּרְכַּ֣ת אֹ֭בֵד עָלַ֣י תָּבֹ֑א וְלֵ֖ב אַלְמָנָ֣ה אַרְנִֽן׃
records.gloss: [The] blessing of [one] about to perish on me came, and [the] heart of [the] widow I made sing for joy.
pieces: The blessing of those who were about to perish came upon me, \q and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.

L.13: [The] blessing of [one] about to perish came upon me, \q and I made [the] widow's heart sing for joy.

R.13: People who were close to dying blessed me, \q and I made widows' hearts sing for joy.

decisions.choice: the blessing of one about to perish: the thanks and good wishes of someone near ruin or death, whom Job helped
decisions.reason: The person was "perishing", lost or dying (31:19; Deuteronomy 26:5; Proverbs 31:6), and blessed Job for saving them. The blessing here is real, not the cover word for cursing used in the prologue (1:5).

decisions.choice: the widow: a woman left without a husband's support
decisions.reason: In Israel widows and orphans had no one to defend their rights and were the law's chief concern (Exodus 22:22; Deuteronomy 24:17). Eliphaz had accused Job of sending widows away empty (22:9).

decisions.choice: those who were about to perish (B); people ... widows (R)
decisions.reason: The singulars stand for every such person; Balanced and Readable use plurals.

records.source: צֶ֣דֶק לָ֭בַשְׁתִּי וַיִּלְבָּשֵׁ֑נִי כִּֽמְעִ֥יל וְ֝צָנִ֗יף מִשְׁפָּטִֽי׃
records.gloss: Righteousness I put on, and it clothed me; like a robe and a turban [was] my justice.
pieces: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; \q my justice was like a robe and a turban.

L.14: I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; \q my justice [was] like a robe and a turban.

R.14: Doing right was like the clothes I wore every day; \q being fair was my robe and my turban.

decisions.choice: put on righteousness ... it clothed me: right conduct was part of him, seen by all
decisions.reason: Clothing pictures what marks a person and shows outwardly (Psalm 132:9; Isaiah 59:17; 61:10). The second verb turns the picture round: righteousness put Job on, as the Spirit "clothed itself" with Gideon (Judges 6:34). Job and right conduct were inseparable.

decisions.choice: righteousness and justice: doing right by others and giving fair judgment
decisions.reason: Righteousness (tsedeq) is right conduct, especially toward others; justice (mishpat) here is the fair decision of cases, which Job gave when he sat at the gate (verses 7, 16). The pair is often joined (Psalm 89:15; Isaiah 9:6).

decisions.choice: robe and turban: the clothes of a person of rank
decisions.reason: The robe (me'il) was an outer garment of honor (1:20; 1 Samuel 18:4); the turban (tsanif) a headdress worn by people of standing (Isaiah 62:3; Zechariah 3:5).

decisions.choice: Doing right ... being fair
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two words mean in practice (m2).

records.source: עֵינַ֣יִם הָ֭יִיתִי לַֽעִוֵּ֑ר וְרַגְלַ֖יִם לַפִּסֵּ֣חַ אָֽנִי׃
records.gloss: Eyes I was to the blind, and feet to the lame [was] I.
pieces: I was eyes for the blind \q and feet for the lame.

L.15: I was eyes to the blind, \q and feet to the lame [was] I.

R.15: I was like eyes for people who were blind \q and like feet for people who could not walk.

decisions.choice: eyes to the blind, feet to the lame: Job supplied what they lacked
decisions.reason: Job guided those who could not see and carried or helped those who could not walk. The law protected the blind (Leviticus 19:14; Deuteronomy 27:18), and Job went beyond protecting them.

decisions.choice: like
decisions.reason: Readable marks the picture as a comparison (m1).

records.source: אָ֣ב אָ֭נֹכִֽי לָֽאֶבְיוֹנִ֑ים וְרִ֖ב לֹא־יָדַ֣עְתִּי אֶחְקְרֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: A father I [was] to the needy, and [the] case of [one] I did not know I searched it out.
pieces: I was a father to the needy, \q and I looked into the case of the stranger.

L.16: I [was] a father to the needy, \q and the case of [the one] I did not know I searched out.

R.16: I cared for poor people like a father, \q and I took the trouble to learn the facts in a stranger's court case.

decisions.choice: the needy: the poor who have to depend on others
decisions.reason: The word ('evyon) means someone in want, poor and easily wronged (5:15; 24:4, 14).

decisions.choice: the case of one I did not know: a stranger's lawsuit
alternatives: a case I did not understand
decisions.reason: Hebrew has "a case [that] I did not know". It most likely means the case of someone Job did not know, a person with no claim on him, whom he still helped (compare 31:32). It could also mean a case whose facts he did not know until he searched them out; either way Job took trouble to see justice done.

decisions.choice: searched out: investigated carefully
decisions.reason: The verb (chaqar) means to search a matter through (5:27; 28:27; Proverbs 25:2). A judge was to inquire carefully before deciding (Deuteronomy 13:15; 19:18).

decisions.choice: the stranger (B); a stranger's court case (R)
alternatives: the one I did not know
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the likelier reading (m2) in plain words.

records.source: וָֽ֭אֲשַׁבְּרָה מְתַלְּע֣וֹת עַוָּ֑ל וּ֝מִשִּׁנָּ֗יו אַשְׁלִ֥יךְ טָֽרֶף׃
records.gloss: And I broke [the] fangs of [the] unjust, and from his teeth I threw [the] prey.
pieces: I broke the fangs of the wicked \q and made them drop their prey from their teeth.

L.17: And I broke the fangs of the unjust, \q and from his teeth I threw [down the] prey.

R.17: I stopped wicked people from hurting others, \q as if I broke a wild animal's jaws \q and pulled its victim from its teeth.

decisions.choice: fangs, teeth, prey: the oppressor pictured as a beast of prey
decisions.reason: The unjust man is pictured as a wild animal with its victim in its jaws (Psalm 3:8; 58:7). Job broke his power and rescued the person he was devouring.

decisions.choice: the unjust: one who does wrong to others
decisions.reason: The word ('avval) means someone who acts unjustly (18:21; 27:7).

decisions.choice: the wicked ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a plural for the class of people meant; the singular in the Hebrew is general.

decisions.choice: I stopped wicked people from hurting others, as if
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means and then keeps it as a comparison (m1). It uses three lines, one for the meaning and two for the picture; the Hebrew has two cola, with a lesser division in the second.

records.source: וָ֭אֹמַר עִם־קִנִּ֣י אֶגְוָ֑ע וְ֝כַח֗וֹל אַרְבֶּ֥ה יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And I said, With my nest I will expire, and like the sand I will multiply days.
pieces: I said, I will die in my own nest, \q and my days will be as many as the grains of sand.

L.18: And I said, I will die with my nest, \q and like the sand I will multiply [my] days.

R.18: I thought, I will die at home with my family around me, \q after a life as long as there are grains of sand.

decisions.choice: die with my nest: die at home, in peace, among my family
alternatives: die in my nest, my home
decisions.reason: A nest pictures a safe home and a brood of young (Numbers 24:21; Obadiah 1:4). Job expected to die old and secure, with his family around him.

decisions.choice: the sand: grains of sand, a picture of a great number
alternatives: the phoenix, a bird said to live for ages
decisions.reason: The word (chol) normally means sand, a common picture of something past counting (6:3; Genesis 22:17). Jewish tradition read it here as the name of a bird that lives a very long time and is born again from its nest, which fits "nest" in the first line; the Hebrew word for sand is the plain reading.

decisions.choice: grains of
decisions.reason: The point of the comparison is number (m2); Balanced and Readable say grains.

records.source: שָׁרְשִׁ֣י פָת֣וּחַ אֱלֵי־מָ֑יִם וְ֝טַ֗ל יָלִ֥ין בִּקְצִירִֽי׃
records.gloss: My root [is] open to [the] water, and dew lodges on my branch.
pieces: My roots reach out to the water, \q and the dew lies all night on my branches.

L.19: My root [is] open to [the] water, \q and [the] dew lodges all night on my branch.

R.19: I was like a tree with roots that reach the water \q and branches wet with dew all night long.

decisions.choice: root and branch: Job pictures himself as a well-watered tree
decisions.reason: A tree by water with dew on it pictures a life that keeps flourishing (8:16; 14:7-9; Psalm 1:3; Jeremiah 17:8). Bildad had said the wicked man's roots dry up and his branch withers (18:16); in the old days Job expected the opposite.

decisions.choice: still part of what Job said to himself
decisions.reason: Verses 19-20 continue the thought begun with "I said" in verse 18, how Job expected his life to go on.

decisions.choice: I was like a tree
decisions.reason: Readable names the picture (m1).

records.source: כְּ֭בוֹדִי חָדָ֣שׁ עִמָּדִ֑י וְ֝קַשְׁתִּ֗י בְּיָדִ֥י תַחֲלִֽיף׃
records.gloss: My glory [is] new with me, and my bow in my hand renews itself.
pieces: My honor stays fresh with me, \q and my bow is ever new in my hand.

L.20: My glory [is] fresh with me, \q and my bow in my hand is renewed.

R.20: People will always respect me, \q and I will stay strong, like a bow that stays new in a warrior's hand.

decisions.choice: my glory: my honor, my standing among people
decisions.reason: The word (kavod) means weight, and so honor and standing. Job said God had stripped his glory from him (19:9).

decisions.choice: my bow renewed: strength that does not fail
decisions.reason: A bow pictures a man's strength (Genesis 49:24; 1 Samuel 2:4); a broken bow is lost power (Psalm 37:15). Job expected his strength to stay fresh.

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: In English "glory" suggests splendor or praise of God; Job means his honor among people (m1). Literal keeps "glory".

decisions.choice: I will stay strong, like a bow
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bow stands for (m2) and keeps the picture as a comparison.

records.source: לִֽי־שָׁמְע֥וּ וְיִחֵ֑לּוּ וְ֝יִדְּמ֗וּ לְמ֣וֹ עֲצָתִֽי׃
records.gloss: To me they listened and waited, and were silent for my counsel.
pieces: People listened to me and waited; \q they kept silent for my advice.

L.21: To me they listened and waited, \q and they kept silent for my counsel.

R.21: People listened to me and waited for me to speak. \q They kept quiet to hear my advice.

decisions.choice: back to what Job's life was like; the people at the gate listen
decisions.reason: After the thoughts of verses 18-20, Job returns to the scene at the city gate (verses 7-10). The verb has no named subject; it means the people who met there.

decisions.choice: counsel: advice on what to do
decisions.reason: The word ('etsah) means advice or a plan; at the gate it means his judgment on the matter in hand. Job had once given counsel; now he hears none (12:13).

decisions.choice: People
decisions.reason: English needs a subject for the verb (m1).

records.source: אַחֲרֵ֣י דְ֭בָרִי לֹ֣א יִשְׁנ֑וּ וְ֝עָלֵ֗ימוֹ תִּטֹּ֥ף מִלָּתִֽי׃
records.gloss: After my word they did not speak again, and on them dropped my speech.
pieces: After I spoke, they did not speak again; \q my words fell on them like drops of rain.

L.22: After my word they did not speak again, \q and my speech dropped upon them.

R.22: When I had spoken, no one had anything to add. \q My words were welcome, like gentle rain.

decisions.choice: they did not speak again: no one added to or argued with Job's word
decisions.reason: The verb (shanah) means to repeat or do again. Job's word was the last word; it settled the matter.

decisions.choice: my speech dropped on them: his words refreshed them like rain
decisions.reason: The verb (nataf) is used of rain dripping (Judges 5:4) and of speech that falls on its hearers like dew or rain (Deuteronomy 32:2). Verse 23 goes on with the picture of rain.

decisions.choice: like drops of rain (B); like gentle rain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the picture clear (m2), which verse 23 continues.

records.source: וְיִֽחֲל֣וּ כַמָּטָ֣ר לִ֑י וּ֝פִיהֶ֗ם פָּעֲר֥וּ לְמַלְקֽוֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: And they waited like for rain for me, and their mouth they opened wide for [the] spring rain.
pieces: They waited for me as for the rain \q and opened their mouths wide as for the spring rain.

L.23: And they waited for me as for [the] rain, \q and they opened their mouth wide as for [the] spring rain.

R.23: They waited for me to speak the way farmers wait for rain. \q They were as eager as dry ground is for the spring showers.

decisions.choice: the spring rain: the last rains of the season, which ripen the crops
decisions.reason: The word (malqosh) names the late rains of March and April, which fill out the grain before harvest; without them the crop fails (Deuteronomy 11:14; Proverbs 16:15; Jeremiah 3:3).

decisions.choice: opened their mouth wide: waited eagerly, like dry ground for rain
decisions.reason: The picture is of thirsty ground opening to the rain, or of people gaping to catch it (Psalm 119:131). They longed for Job's words.

decisions.choice: the way farmers wait ... as eager as dry ground
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of the open mouth (m2) instead of reproducing it.

records.source: אֶשְׂחַ֣ק אֲ֭לֵהֶם לֹ֣א יַאֲמִ֑ינוּ וְא֥וֹר פָּ֝נַ֗י לֹ֣א יַפִּילֽוּן׃
records.gloss: I laughed to them, they did not believe; and [the] light of my face they did not make fall.
pieces: I smiled on them when they had lost confidence, \q and they did not cast down the light of my face.

L.24: I smiled at them [when] they did not believe, \q and the light of my face they did not cast down.

R.24: When people lost hope, I smiled at them and encouraged them. \q They could not make me lose my cheerful look.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: Job smiled on them when they had lost heart
alternatives: they could hardly believe it, that so great a man would smile at them
if I smiled at them, they did not take it lightly
decisions.reason: The line is hard. "Did not believe" most likely means they had no confidence and Job's smile encouraged them. It could also mean they could hardly believe that Job would smile on them, so highly did they regard him. Both fit the honor described in verses 21-25.

decisions.choice: the light of my face: a friendly, favoring look
decisions.reason: A shining face shows favor and goodwill (Psalm 4:7; Proverbs 16:15, which joins it with the spring rain of verse 23). "They did not cast it down" means that nothing they did made Job's goodwill fail, or that they did not let it fall unheeded.

decisions.choice: and encouraged them; my cheerful look
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what the smile and the light of the face meant (m1, m2).

records.source: אֶֽבֲחַ֣ר דַּרְכָּם֮ וְאֵשֵׁ֪ב רֹ֥אשׁ וְ֭אֶשְׁכּוֹן כְּמֶ֣לֶךְ בַּגְּד֑וּד כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אֲבֵלִ֣ים יְנַחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: I chose their way and sat [as] chief, and I dwelt like a king among the troop, as [one] who comforts mourners.
pieces: I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; \q I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts those who mourn.

L.25: I chose their way and sat [as] chief, \q and I dwelt like a king among [his] troops, as one who comforts mourners.

R.25: I decided what they should do and sat as their leader. \q I was like a king with his army, and like someone who comforts people in grief.

decisions.choice: chose their way: decided what course they should take
alternatives: chose to go their way, to visit them
decisions.reason: Job led his community: he decided the course they would follow, as a chief does. Some take it as "I chose to go to them", but the next words, "sat as chief", point to leadership.

decisions.choice: like a king among his troops: honored and in command
decisions.reason: A king among his army is the picture of unquestioned leadership. Job ends the picture of his past greatness with a gentle line: he was also like one who comforts mourners. His friends came to comfort him and failed (2:11; 16:2).

decisions.choice: the past ends here; chapter 30 begins "But now"
decisions.reason: Chapter 29 is all memory. Chapter 30 sets the present against it, beginning "And now" (30:1, 9, 16).

decisions.choice: for them; his troops (B); his army (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that Job chose the way on their behalf (m1) and that the troops are the king's.
